what_this_is: The phase-E answer: the frozen set of 32 analyses, run on the development period and again on the held-out year, reported side by side. The pairing was fixed in batch 15 before the year was opened.

how_hard_the_year_was.note: The denominator of every skill score, on a model nobody here tuned. Raw CRPS is not comparable across the two datasets -- different year, four splits rather than eight, 192 cells rather than 371 -- and this is the figure that says so.

the_two_spreads.note: Each dataset's noise band is measured on that dataset, from its own four repeats of the unseeded reference.

does_the_ordering_transfer.note: Whether an analysis that scored better on development scores better on 2010. This is the question a development-set ranking is used for, and it is answered here rather than assumed.

the_gap.note: Holdout skill minus development skill, per analysis. A negative value is an analysis that did better on the data it was developed against than on the year it had never seen.

rows_not_paired.development: the main path's own choice, run under its own name; the same analysis as `main`
rows_not_paired.holdout: not run: its development twin has no conclusion (frozen; the main path's own choice, run under its own name; the same analysis as `main`)

frozen_pairing_verified.note: Every development figure in the frozen manifest still equals what the development table says. If it did not, this script would have stopped rather than reported the comparison.
